decisions.question: How are the phase's declarations cut into at most 6 tasks, each test-first except the last?

options.label: 5 tasks: purity hardening, IR, DSL main part, plan library, gate
options.consequence: each task carries its own red-green cycle and a reviewable seam; the IR lands before the DSL, whose buildDefinition() names TopologyDefinition; the plan library and exports test land together when both export lists become final

options.label: 4 tasks: purity hardening, IR, the whole DSL library, gate
options.consequence: one task of about 500 lines of library code and both public libraries; a reviewer cannot approve the main-library DSL while rejecting the plan classes

options.label: 6 tasks: the above with the stage classes split from the plan
options.consequence: a stage task without its visitor and plan has no fixture of its own to turn green, so its failing test would be contrived

decisions.chosen: 5 tasks: purity hardening, IR, DSL main part, plan library, gate
decisions.why: The fixtures fall along these seams: ir_holds_no_function.dart turns green at Task 2, topologies.dart and eight reject libraries at Task 3, plan.dart and dsl_types_are_closed.dart at Task 4, so every task's failing step is a real replay or test state the dry run recorded. The routed purity hardening is its own task so it lands before any new library (the routed item says so).

decisions.question: How are topology-ir@v1's The IR and Function references split into files under lib/src/ir/?

options.label: one library per Interface section: definition.dart and function_ref.dart
options.consequence: follows nidana.model.3's one-library-per-section layout; EdgeInput's sealed family shares definition.dart as Dart requires; nidana.model.10 and .11 add the canonical orders and the projection as further files

options.label: one file ir.dart
options.consequence: a 150-line file mixing FunctionRef, which nidana.model.10 fills on its own, with the edge rules

options.label: three files: edge.dart, definition.dart, function_ref.dart
options.consequence: splits one Interface section across two files with no phase that edits them apart

decisions.chosen: one library per Interface section: definition.dart and function_ref.dart
decisions.why: Precedent of nidana.model.3 (one library per Interface section under lib/src/topic/) and D4's one directory per area; the Interface's own sections give the seam.

decisions.question: Which part files make up the DSL library lib/src/topology/topology.dart (D4: one library with part files)?

options.label: library file with Topologies and Pipeline values; parts builder, handle, plan, stages, sinks
options.consequence: each part holds one Interface group; nidana.model.9 edits builder, handle, plan and stages, nidana.model.11 plan.dart's definition getter, without touching the others

options.label: library file plus two parts (main-library names, plan names)
options.consequence: two files of 200 to 300 lines each, the builder and the handle together, the stages with the visitors

options.label: one file per class
options.consequence: about 25 part files, most of them three lines of declarations

decisions.chosen: library file with Topologies and Pipeline values; parts builder, handle, plan, stages, sinks
decisions.why: Focused files with one responsibility each (writing-plans File Structure); the sealed TopicStream and PlanSink with their subclasses must share the library, which parts allow. The library file carries every import, which the dry run showed serves all five parts with no unused import.

decisions.question: What are the export lists of the main library and topology_plan.dart, and how are they written?

options.label: show lists over the one DSL library: main library 40 names, topology_plan.dart 27
options.consequence: the main library adds export 'src/ir/definition.dart' show (6 names), 'src/ir/function_ref.dart' show FunctionRef, 'src/topology/topology.dart' show (8 names); topology_plan.dart exports the same DSL library showing the plan's 27 names; disjoint by construction of the lists

options.label: bare exports of per-library files
options.consequence: impossible for the DSL: one library holds both libraries' names, so a bare export would leak the plan into the main library

decisions.chosen: show lists over the one DSL library: main library 40 names, topology_plan.dart 27
decisions.why: The DSL is one library (D4), so only show lists can split it between the two public libraries (G2); nidana.model.3 already uses show lists for every export.

decisions.question: How is 'the main library exports exactly the declarations the three contracts place in it' checked: a checklist grep as nidana.model.3 did, or a test?

options.label: a test, exports_test.dart, reading both libraries' show lists
options.consequence: every later gate keeps both lists exact (a leak of visitStage or ReadStage into the main library fails); nidana.model.5 edits neither library, so the test stays true; costs about 95 lines

options.label: a checklist grep in the verification task
options.consequence: checked once, at this phase's gate; a later phase can leak a name past the three names plan_is_a_separate_library.dart checks

decisions.chosen: a test, exports_test.dart, reading both libraries' show lists
decisions.why: writing-plans asks for a test behind each Review Focus line, and the reject set covers only MapStage, TopologyPlan and planOf; D4 Restated makes both lists final at this phase, so a test can pin them without later edits.

decisions.question: Where do workspaceRoot() and packageDirectory() live once exports_test.dart also needs them?

options.label: move them to test/src/package_files.dart (Task 1)
options.consequence: one definition, imported by purity_test.dart and exports_test.dart; dart test runs only *_test.dart, so the helper is never a test

options.label: import 'purity_test.dart' show packageDirectory from exports_test.dart
options.consequence: no move, but a test file imported as a library, which reads oddly

options.label: duplicate the 15 lines in exports_test.dart
options.consequence: two copies of the D6 root-finding rule to keep in step

decisions.question: How far does the routed purity-test hardening go: the three gaps the routed item names, or every URI spelling the probe finds?

options.label: the routed three plus part directives, adjacent literals, escapes and other schemes
options.consequence: the reader joins adjacent literals, reads part and part of, rejects a backslash and any scheme but dart and package; the probe shows 'dart:' 'io' and 'dart:\x69o' both import dart:io; about 15 more lines

options.label: the routed three only
options.consequence: two spellings that import dart:io stay invisible to the G25 test while part files land

decisions.chosen: the routed three plus part directives, adjacent literals, escapes and other schemes
decisions.why: The probe settled that both spellings resolve (no analyzer issue), and this phase lands the first part files and relative imports, so the reader must read part directives to check them at all. Each extra rule is one line and has a self-test case and a seeded violation in the dry run.

decisions.question: What does Task 1's failing step look like, given that the readers under test live in the test file?

options.label: new self-tests and G-test bodies against the old readers: a compile failure naming the new API
options.consequence: one red step: 'No named parameter with the name path' twice and 'Method not found: effectsIn' four times; the reader gaps themselves are shown by the dry run's seeded violations

options.label: two red-green cycles, the directive reader first with its old signature
options.consequence: an assertion-level failure for directiveUris, then a compile failure for allowedUri and effectsIn; two more steps for the same deliverable

decisions.chosen: new self-tests and G-test bodies against the old readers: a compile failure naming the new API
decisions.why: The brief allows a test-first change of the test file; one red step keeps the task to the template's five steps, and T1.5 records that the hardened test fails on each seeded spelling.

decisions.question: D3 wants a final field behind every getter and throwing bodies: which private constructors does the analyzer report as unused, and how is that handled?

options.label: two ignores of unused_element, on TransformEdge._ and TopologyDefinition._
options.consequence: matches nidana.model.3's RedactedPayload._; the stage, sink, builder and plan constructors need none, because a private constructor that is its class's only constructor is not reported; nidana.model.10 removes both ignores

options.label: factories that construct through the private constructor without validation
options.consequence: no ignore, but a factory whose contract is validation and an unmodifiable copy would return unvalidated values before nidana.model.10

options.label: a file-level ignore_for_file
options.consequence: hides any other unused element in definition.dart

decisions.chosen: two ignores of unused_element, on TransformEdge._ and TopologyDefinition._
decisions.why: The probe shows exactly which constructors are reported (only one beside a factory); precedent S106 took the same line-local suppression for the same pattern.

decisions.question: FunctionRef.named(String name) 'Throws ArgumentError for an empty [name]': does this phase store the name, check it, or throw UnimplementedError?

options.label: store the name (FunctionRef.named(String this.name)); the check is nidana.model.10's
options.consequence: a generative constructor that stores its argument, as nidana.model.3's MessageEnvelope did before its copy landed; the dartdoc's ArgumentError holds from nidana.model.10

options.label: check and throw ArgumentError now
options.consequence: delivers part of nidana.model.10's FunctionRef behavior early, against topology-ir@v1's Delivery

options.label: throw UnimplementedError in the initializer
options.consequence: the surface fixture's FunctionRef.named('search') would throw if ever run, and the constructor stores nothing

decisions.chosen: store the name (FunctionRef.named(String this.name)); the check is nidana.model.10's
decisions.why: topology-ir@v1 Delivery gives FunctionRef to nidana.model.10; nidana.model.3's plan delivered members that store an argument. The probe confirms a String initializing formal over a String? field is accepted.

decisions.question: TransformEdge.isSink is output != null: delivered now or thrown, and are TopologyDefinition.reads and .writes final fields or getters?

options.label: isSink and isStateBearing throw; reads and writes are final fields
options.consequence: follows nidana.model.3, whose Topic.ref threw although derivable; D3's final field behind every getter covers reads and writes, which nidana.model.10's factory derives at construction

options.label: isSink delivered; reads and writes throwing getters
options.consequence: an early sliver of nidana.model.10's edge rules, and two getters without fields against D3

decisions.chosen: isSink and isStateBearing throw; reads and writes are final fields
decisions.why: D3 and nidana.model.3's precedent; topology-ir@v1 Delivery gives TransformEdge's rules to nidana.model.10.

decisions.question: The Interface writes 'sealed class EdgeInput {}' with no constructor and no annotation, while the prose makes every value type @immutable and TopicInput and StageInput have const constructors. What does EdgeInput declare?

options.label: @immutable sealed class EdgeInput with const EdgeInput._()
options.consequence: the const subclasses compile (an implicit default constructor is not const, the probe shows const_constructor_with_non_const_super), EdgeInput has no public constructor, and the annotation covers both subclasses as MessageSource's does

options.label: the block as written
options.consequence: const TopicInput(...) and const StageInput(...) do not compile

decisions.chosen: @immutable sealed class EdgeInput with const EdgeInput._()
decisions.why: The probe settles the const question; the prose above the Interface asks for @immutable on every value type; MessageSource is the precedent for a sealed base with a const private constructor.

decisions.question: The trailing comments of TopologyDefinition.reads and .writes push their lines past 80 columns, and the formatter then splits each declaration after its type. Keep them trailing, or move them?

options.label: move those two comments to the line above their fields
options.consequence: the comment text is kept as written; the two declarations read on one line each

options.label: keep them trailing
options.consequence: the formatter writes 'final Set<TopicRef>' and 'reads; // ...' on two lines

decisions.chosen: move those two comments to the line above their fields

decisions.why: The comment describes the Interface's shorthand, not the code; every other Interface comment is carried.
